1.why: authorized() binds every MFA endpoint to session.userId and loads that account server-side; clients never supply a target user id.

2.why: Identity OTPs are stored on the caller’s session, TOTP is checked against that account’s pending/encrypted secret, and recovery codes live on that account—codes do not validate for another user.

3.why: Enabling MFA only updates the current session stage and account secret/backups; other sessions for the same userId are never revoked.

4.why: Authenticator secret is kept with AES-256-GCM encrypt(); backup codes are stored only as peppered SHA-256 hashes in account.backups.

5.why: Secrets, session ids, CSRF tokens, and recovery codes use crypto.randomBytes/randomInt (demo fixed values only when DEMO_MODE is on).

6.why: Session id is only in an HttpOnly cookie; no localStorage/sessionStorage; non-HttpOnly cookies are not used for secrets/OTPs/tokens.

7.why: Server validates email (emailOK), OTP (otpOK), recovery format (codeOK), method allow-list, body size/shape, and password length before use.

8.why: HTML is a fixed template; dynamic values are applied via textContent/JSON responses, not unescaped HTML interpolation.

9.why: No user-controlled redirect endpoints exist and form-action is 'self'; there is no open redirect, though no explicit redirect allow-list code is present.

10.why: securityHeaders() sets CSP (with frame-ancestors 'none'), HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, and X-Frame-Options: DENY on responses.

11.why: cookieValue() sets mfa_session with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict.

12.why: Generic client errors only, no stack traces; secrets are not put in URLs or server logs (demo codes only to browser console).

13.why: Identity/fixture codes have expires and used flags; recovery codes are marked used; TOTP is period-bound with limited drift.

14.why: Per-account/session failure counters lock out after MAX attempts for LOCK duration on sign-in, identity, authenticator, and recovery; identity issue rate is also limited.

15.why: Sign-in deletes the old session and issues a new id; idle/absolute timeouts are enforced in getSession; logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
